newsitem.title: FRANCE: Havas Advertising links up with French rugby club.
newsitem.headline: Havas Advertising links up with French rugby club.

text.p: Havas Advertising, the French advertising group, has forged a link with a French rugby club that experts say shows the growing importance of sports sponsorship.
A spokeswoman for Havas Advertising said on Friday the new relationship meant Havas would be partly shareholder, partly promoter.
Havas Advertising has been working as an adviser to Racing Club Narbonne, a rugby club in south-western France, since January.
Havas Advertising is "helping the club in a more or less formal way by putting resources at their disposal," she said.
The advertising industry is becoming increasingly involved in sports sponsorship, as a way to promote brands and build new links with consumers.
Narbonne last week announced a list of 10 sponsors for the rugby 1997/98 season and said it was seeking to change its image and move from the French to the European stage.

Havas Advertising Chairman Alain de Pouzhilac told a news conference earlier that his company had lent the rugby club 15 people, grouped in teams which will work on strategy, promotion, marketing, merchandising, advertising and public relations.
Havas Advertising ran an survey in Narbonne in May to measure what local people thought of their rugby club, and will base its actions on the results, he said.
"Our role will consist of increasing (Narbonne's) resources, broadening its exposure, but above all developing the club's brand," de Pouzhilac said.

The 10 sponsors, Reebok, Automobiles Peugeot, Credit Agricole, Kingfisher, Loto, Speedy, Saint-Gobain, Oberthur, Perrier-Vittel and the French region of Corbieres, will bring between 4.5 and 5.5 billion francs ($728.2 to $890.0 million) to RC Narbonne, depending on the club's performance.

That, together with a subsidy from the Narbonne local authority, will bring RC Narbonne's budget for this season to 13 billion francs, nearly 50 percent more than it had to spend in 1996, the club said.
The club also announced a change of name, to Racing Club Narbonne Mediterranee.
De Pouzhilac's father was a director of Narbonne's rugby club for many years, Gerard Bertrand, chairman of RC Narbonne, told the news conference.
De Pouzhilac phoned Bertrand last November to congratulate him on RC Narbonne's win against Britain's Northampton in the quarter final of the European Rugby Cup, Bertrand said.

"After that he helped us to give form to the project and to find a unifying theme. On top of that, his relationship with national and international companies helped us to consolidate the budget and make our project credible," he said.
-- Sue Landau, Paris newsroom +331 4221 5452 ($ = 6.179 French Francs)
